lines.en: It is no exaggeration to say that advertising shapes what we want without us noticing.
The campaign is said to have cost millions, yet nobody remembers the product it promoted.
What makes an advertisement memorable is rarely its budget, but the story it tells.
Not only do advertisers sell products, but they also sell dreams and lifestyles.
However careful you are, it is almost impossible to escape advertisements in a modern city.
Were newspapers to disappear completely, something important would be lost from our daily lives.
It is often the quietest message in an advertisement that influences us the most.
The report claims that children see thousands of advertisements before they are old enough to understand them.
Rarely does a news story today appear without some opinion mixed into the facts.
What we should teach children is not to avoid media, but to question it.
It is widely felt that the line between news and entertainment has become dangerously blurred.
Had the headline been checked before publication, the false story would never have spread so far.
What makes a slogan stick is its rhythm, not the product it describes.
Rarely do viewers realize how carefully an apparently spontaneous video has been planned.
The more time we spend online, the harder it becomes to tell whether our opinions are truly our own.
